title: Describing things
job: Size, colour, quality — agreement at length
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: un beau + N   /   un bel + N-vowel

rules.text: AGREEMENT HERE IS ALMOST ENTIRELY A WRITING RULE: -e for the feminine, -s for the plural, -es for both — grand, grande, grands, grandes, where three of the four sound identical. An adjective already ending in -e adds nothing for gender (rouge, jaune, jeune), and one already ending in -s adds nothing for the plural (gris, français). A learner who cannot hear it will not believe it matters; the index does, because grand and grande are two different keys.

THE ADJECTIVE NORMALLY FOLLOWS THE NOUN — une voiture rouge, un livre intéressant — which is the reverse of English. A small closed set goes in front: beau, joli, jeune, vieux, bon, mauvais, grand, petit, gros, nouveau. The summary people remember is beauty, age, goodness, size; the true statement is that it is a LIST, and the list is what to learn.

Three of those front adjectives have a THIRD shape before a masculine noun starting with a vowel: beau → bel, nouveau → nouvel, vieux → vieil. un bel appartement, un nouvel ami, un vieil homme. It is the same instinct as M2's mon amie — French avoids the vowel clash and changes the spelling to do it — and each shape is its own index key.

Two colours refuse to bend at all: marron and orange are nouns doing an adjective's work — a chestnut, an orange — so les chaussures marron keeps its shape. blanc goes to blanche, which is irregular; rouge, jaune and rose mark number only; bleu, vert, noir and gris take all four cells.

très modifies an ADJECTIVE and beaucoup modifies a VERB. très grand, j'aime beaucoup — and très j'aime is the error an English speaker makes, because "very" and "very much" look like one word with a tail. It is the same pair Spanish teaches as muy and mucho.

words.note: It ends in -e already, so it never marks gender — une voiture rouge, un livre rouge. Only the plural adds anything.
The same shape as rouge: number only. The j is the soft zh of French, and the au is a single o sound.

sentences.trap: Nothing happens here for gender, and that is a fact about this adjective rather than about French. bleue and verte would both have moved.
sentences.sound: la vwa-TÜR eh ROOZH. The final e is silent and the g before it is the soft zh.

variations.changed: a masculine noun — and rouge does not move
a different colour of the same class
plural, where rouge finally does add something

mistake.why: One car takes the singular: La voiture est rouge.

sentences.usage: Naming which one you mean, in a car park or a shop.
sentences.mnemonic: An -e adjective marks number and nothing else.

words.note: All four cells, and all four sound the same. The written agreement is real and invisible, which is the module's whole point.
M2 opened this row for eyes; here it is a colour in general. The feminine sounds its t and the masculine does not.
Four cells, and the r is sounded in all of them. The oi is a single wa sound.

sentences.trap: bleus, bleue and bleues are all said the same as bleu. French writes four forms and pronounces one, which is why the spelling has to be learnt separately from the word.
sentences.sound: lay LEEVR son BLUH. The eu is the rounded vowel, and no final letter is heard.

variations.changed: feminine plural — four letters more, no sound
a colour whose r IS heard
singular, and a silent t

mistake.why: The plural is written even when it is not heard: Les livres sont bleus.

words.note: Its feminine is blanche, not blanque or blance — the c becomes ch and the vowel before it changes sound. Irregular, and worth holding as a word.
INVARIABLE, because it is the noun for a chestnut. les chaussures marron keeps its shape whatever it describes — and orange behaves the same way.

sentences.trap: The adjective comes AFTER the noun here, which is the ordinary French order and the reverse of English. Only the small front list breaks it.
sentences.sound: say ün vwa-TÜR BLAHNSH. The an of blanche is nasal and the ch is a sh.

variations.changed: masculine — and the c goes silent
an invariable colour
plural, with the indefinite des

mistake.why: Colours follow the noun: C'est une voiture blanche.

sentences.mnemonic: Colours go behind. Only the short list goes in front.

words.note: One of the front list. Its plural is beaux with an x rather than an s, which a handful of -eau words do.
The feminine, and it shares almost nothing with beau on the page. It is a different shape rather than an ending.
Also in the front list, and regular. It is lighter than beau — a pretty dress rather than a beautiful one.

sentences.trap: beau goes in FRONT because it is on the list, and rouge goes behind because it is not. There is no principle to work it out from — the list is the rule.
sentences.sound: say un bo LEEVR. beau is one syllable, and the au is a pure o.

variations.changed: feminine, and a different shape entirely
a lighter word from the same list
plural — and des becomes de in front of an adjective

mistake.why: beau is on the front list: C'est un beau livre.

sentences.usage: Praising something, which is what most of the front list is for.
sentences.mnemonic: The list goes in front. Everything else goes behind.

words.note: Masculine and starting with a vowel, which is exactly why it pulls bel in front of it. The double p is written and not heard.
beau's third shape, used only in front of a masculine noun starting with a vowel. It is its own index key, not a variant of beau.
The same pattern as beau, including the -x plural. Its feminine nouvelle also shares little with it on the page.
nouveau's pre-vowel shape — un nouvel ami. Three of these exist in the language and this module has all three.

sentences.trap: bel exists only in front of a vowel and only in the masculine. Move the adjective behind the noun and it goes back to beau — the shape belongs to the position, not to the word.
sentences.sound: say un bel a-par-tuh-MON. The l of bel links straight onto the vowel.

variations.changed: the second of the three pre-vowel shapes
feminine — where the problem never arises
a consonant, so the ordinary shape

mistake.why: A vowel takes bel: C'est un bel appartement.

sentences.mnemonic: Three words have a pre-vowel shape. These are all of them.

words.note: The h is silent and French counts the word as beginning with a vowel — l'homme, un vieil homme. femme is its pair, and only one of them is said the way it looks.
The third pre-vowel shape, and it appears in front of an h too — homme starts with a silent h, which French treats as a vowel.
M2 opened this beside vieux. The ille is the soft y of fille.
On the front list, and its masculine plural is also mauvais — it already ends in s. bon's opposite.

sentences.trap: The h of homme is silent and French counts it as a vowel. So vieil, not vieux — and the rule is about sound rather than spelling, as it always is here.
sentences.sound: say un vyay OM. The h is not said at all, and vieil links straight into the vowel.

variations.changed: feminine
a consonant, so the ordinary shape
a different front-list adjective

mistake.why: A silent h counts as a vowel: C'est un vieil homme.

sentences.usage: Describing a person by age, and the shape is the point.
sentences.mnemonic: A silent h is a vowel to French.

words.note: Bulk rather than height. Of a person it means fat and is blunt, which is why grand covers most of what English's "big" does.
Its feminine adds a u to keep the g hard: longue. The masculine's g is not sounded at all.

sentences.trap: très goes with an adjective and beaucoup goes with a verb. très grande and j'aime beaucoup — putting très in front of a verb is the error, and it comes straight from English's "very much".
sentences.sound: treh GRAHND. The feminine sounds the d; the masculine grand does not.

variations.changed: masculine, with a silent g
bulk rather than size

variations.cue: I like the house very much
variations.changed: a verb, so beaucoup

mistake.why: A verb takes beaucoup: J'aime beaucoup la maison.

sentences.mnemonic: très with an adjective, beaucoup with a verb.

words.note: Length, never height. A short person is petit — M2's word — and using court of a person is the error.

sentences.trap: cheveux is plural in French, so its adjective is plural too. English says "the hair is short" with a singular, and the two languages disagree about how many hairs there are.

a singular masculine thing

words.note: BEHIND the noun it means clean; in FRONT of it, it means "own" — ma propre voiture is my own car. Position changes the meaning outright.
propre's opposite, and an -e adjective. It is nothing to do with the English word it is spelled like.
L1-M7 opened the singular; the plural is new. It is feminine, so its adjectives take an -e whether or not anything is heard.

sentences.trap: Two adjectives change meaning with position and this is one of them. une voiture propre is a clean car; ma propre voiture is my own car, clean or not.
sentences.sound: la TABL eh PROPR. Both words end in a consonant cluster with no vowel after it.

plural
in front of the verb rather than after it

words.note: The d is silent in the masculine and sounded in the feminine lourde — the ordinary French pattern, on one more word.
Its feminine takes a grave accent to keep the sound: légère. Weight only — light as in not dark is clair.

sentences.trap: légère changes its accent as well as adding an e. The acute é becomes grave è, because the syllable is now closed — which is a spelling rule the eye has to learn.
